title: Incident Evidence Retention & Deep-Dive Playbook
author: Priya Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard for evidence retention, packaging, and deep-dive incident reviews. It ties SLO/error-budget signals to evidence collection and capacity planning decisions, prescribes tool integrations and retention windows, and provides a step-by-step runbook for executing a technical deep dive after a production incident.

Scope

- Applies to all customer-facing inference services, routing, and runtime components (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private control plane observability hooks).
- Covers telemetry (metrics, traces, logs), configuration snapshots, model artifacts and quantization profiles, core dumps, and replayable request traces.
- Does not replace legal/regulated eDiscovery requirements; escalate to Security & Legal for retention overrides.

Key definitions

- SLO: A service-level objective expressed as an availability/latency/accuracy target (e.g., 99.9% 99th percentile inference latency under normal load).
- Error budget: The allowable deviation from the SLO expressed as a percentage/time window.
- Evidence artifact: Any on-disk or object-store item produced during/after an incident used for root cause analysis (logs, traces, metrics slices, config snapshots, binary artifacts).

Guiding principles

1) Evidence must be sufficient to replay or reproduce the failure mode at timeframes defined below.
2) Retention windows should balance forensic usefulness against storage cost and data residency policies.
3) SLO and error-budget signals determine the priority, retention extension, and capacity actions.
4) Automation first: collection and packaging should be reproducible with a CLI or single-click in our incident tooling.

Evidence retention policy (table)

- Use the table below as the canonical retention defaults. Operations or Security may request extensions (see "Retention extension procedure").

Artifact type | Default retention | Retention extension trigger | Storage location
------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------------
Metrics (time series) | 13 months (raw), 36 months (downsampled) | Any major SLO breach > 1% monthly budget burn or regulatory need | Metrics-archive-{region} (long-term TSDB)
Trace spans | 90 days | Incident with P0/P1 or evidence request from Legal/Security | Traces-bucket (tempo-compatible)
Structured logs (full) | 30 days | SLO breach > 0.5% or manual extension by Evidence Lead | Loki/{cluster}/raw-logs
Log index (light) | 13 months | N/A | Logs-index-{region}
Config snapshots (models, runtime flags, kernel versions) | 2 years | Always retained for incidents categorized as "config regression" | Config-store/incident-manifests/{incident-id}
Model artifacts & quantization profiles | 5 years (or customer retention spec) | Customer-sensitive incidents or compliance requests | Models-archive/{model-id}
Core dumps / heap dumps | 90 days (encrypted at rest) | Required for crash RCA | Forensics-bucket (restricted access)
Replayable request traces (raw request + response) | 21 days | If trace correlates with SLO breach or is from VIP customer | Request-replay-store (access-logged)
Incident-artifact bundle (tar.gz) | 2 years | Always retained for P0/P1 incidents | Incident-bundles/{incident-id} (immutable)

Retention extension procedure

1) Any incident owner or Evidence Lead may request extension via the Incident Management UI -> "Extend Evidence Retention" with reason, TTL, and approver.
2) Security/Legal must approve extensions that touch customer PII or regulated data.
3) Operations will implement the extension and emit an audit record (who, why, until when).

Deep-dive triage checklist (runbook)

Trigger: A post-incident review is required when an incident is P0/P1, when an SLO burns > 5% of its monthly error budget in a single day, or when customer-facing regressions occur.

Step 1 — Declare evidence lead and scope (0–30 minutes after triage)
- Incident Commander (IC) assigns an Evidence Lead.
- Evidence Lead records the incident-id tag and target timeframe to preserve (start_ts, end_ts).
- Capture current config snapshot: runtime flags, model hash, kernel versions, autoscaler revision. CLI: redwoodctl incident snapshot --id={incident-id} --out=/tmp/snap-{id}.json

Step 2 — Lock and tag artifacts (30–90 minutes)
- Use the Incident Artifact CLI to create an immutable bundle: redwoodctl incident bundle --id={incident-id} --include=logs,metrics,traces,configs --ttl=2y
- Tag the bundle with SLO metadata: slo_name, slo_window, budget_consumed_percent.

Step 3 — Surface correlated signals (90–180 minutes)
- Query Prometheus/TSDB to extract SLO contribution by tenant and region. Example PromQL to compute 99th latency error budget contribution: 100 * sum(increase(slo_latency_exceedance_count{service="inference-api"}[1d])) / sum(increase(slo_request_count{service="inference-api"}[1d]))
- Extract trace sample set for requests that crossed the latency threshold: tempo query "service:inference-api AND duration>1500ms AND timestamp:[start TO end]"

Step 4 — Reproduction & capacity rehearsal (4–24 hours)
- If reproducible, use the replay store to run a controlled replay against a staging instance with identical model hash and runtime flags. Use isolated tenant quotas to avoid noisy neighbors.
- If reproduction not possible, collect additional high-fidelity metrics (per-core GPU utilization, kernel stall counters, NVLink errors) for another 48–72 hours.

Step 5 — Root cause hypothesis and validation (1–3 days)
- Use a hypothesis log: one-line hypothesis, evidence-to-date, missing evidence, validation step, and result. Update the incident bundle with intermediate artifacts.

SLO & error-budget correlation matrix (operational triggers)

- Advisory: Monthly error budget burn > 0.5% in 24h -> Pager to SRE lead for observation.
- Action: Monthly error budget burn > 2% in 24h -> Immediate focused triage, create deep-dive ticket and preserve evidence for 90 days minimum.
- Escalation: Monthly error budget burn > 5% in 24h or single-day SLO breaches affecting > 10% of customers -> Trigger P1 incident cadence, preserve full incident bundle immutable for 2 years, capacity hedging (see below).

Capacity hedging checklist (when SLO triggers require capacity action)

1) Verify autoscaling history: retrieve last 3 hours of scaler decisions (redwoodctl autoscale history --service inference --window 3h).
2) If autoscaler failed to scale due to GPU provisioning limit, open a capacity request to Cloud Infra with target GPU count and justification.
3) If latency tail caused by scheduling jitter (quantization hot-path), temporarily route VIP traffic to a lower-quantized model variant using routing policy: rtx-route set --service inference --from=prod --to=model-v1-quantized-safe --weight=100 --duration=1h
4) Post-hedge, monitor error budget burn and 95/99 latency percentiles for 2 hours before removing the hedge.

Operational tooling & integration patterns

- Telemetry: Grafana for dashboards, Prometheus/Thanos for metrics, Tempo for traces, Loki for logs. Centralized dashboards must include SLO burn rate panels, tenant-level percentiles, and autoscaler decision traces.
- Evidence bundling: Incident bundles are stored in S3-compatible buckets with server-side encryption (KMS keys per-region). Access to bundles requires incident role and short-lived tokens.
- Automation: Incident playbooks should be executable via CI: .github/actions/incident-packaging to generate artifact bundles automatically when a new incident is created.
- Audit: Every evidence access must write an immutable audit event to the evidence-audit log and send a notification to #incident-evidence channel.

Queries and CLI examples

- PromQL: Compute 99th tail error budget contribution for last 24h:
  100 * sum(increase(slo_latency_exceedance_count{service=\"inference-api\"}[24h])) / sum(increase(slo_request_count{service=\"inference-api\"}[24h]))

- Trace extraction (Tempo):
  tempo query "service:inference-api AND duration>1200ms AND http.status>=500" --from={start} --to={end} --out=slow-traces.json

- Bundle creation:
  redwoodctl incident bundle --id={incident-id} --include logs,metrics,traces,configs,replay --out s3://incident-bundles/{incident-id}.tar.gz --encrypt --tag slo={slo_name},budget={percent}

Incident evidence handoff procedure

1) Evidence Lead packages artifacts and marks the bundle as ready.
2) IC notifies RCA team and posts the bundle link in the incident timeline.
3) RCA team pulls the bundle to an isolated analysis workspace (temporary role granted automatically).
4) All investigators sign the evidence access log and acknowledge the confidentiality requirements.

Post-review actions and runbook (closing loop)

- Within 7 days of deep-dive completion, the RCA lead must:
  - Produce an actionable remediation plan (owner, ETA, verification criteria).
  - Propose SLO or alert tuning if thresholds were inappropriate (include simulation notes).
  - If capacity was insufficient, include proposed capacity commitments (reserved GPUs, autoscaler changes, pre-warm policy).
- Owners must create JIRA tickets labeled incident-{id}-action and attach the incident bundle.
- Evidence retention extension if remediation requires long-term correlation (submit as described above).

Governance and audit

- A monthly "Evidence Audit" is run by SRE Operations to ensure: bundles exist for all P0/P1 incidents, retention tags are correct, and access logs are complete.
- An annual review of default retention windows occurs in Q4 (Ops + Security + Legal) to rebalance cost vs. forensic value.

Appendix A — Sample incident artifact manifest (plain text)

incident_id: INC-2024-0423-42
created_by: ic@redwood.example.com
created_at: 2024-04-23T13:42:00Z
artifacts:
  - name: metrics-slice-99p-20240423-13-42.promql
    path: s3://incident-bundles/INC-2024-0423-42/metrics.prom
  - name: traces-slow-sample.json
    path: s3://incident-bundles/INC-2024-0423-42/traces.json
  - name: config-snapshot.json
    path: s3://config-store/incident-manifests/INC-2024-0423-42.json

Appendix B — Contact matrix

- Incident Commander: Pager on-call SRE (channel: #sre-oncall)
- Evidence Lead: Assigned by IC (role: evidence-lead)
- Forensics/Legal: security-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Capacity requests: cloud-infra@redwood.example.com (subject: Capacity Hedge Request)

Notes and future work

- We plan to prototype immutable evidence bags with verifiable checksums and a WORM storage path for particularly high-sensitivity incidents.
- Investigate 1-click replay-as-test harness integration in staging to reduce manual reproduction overhead.
